title: Janmashtami: the night Krishna was born
hook: a prison at midnight, a river that parts, and a baby carried across it to safety
carry: the avatar comes in the darkest hour
tomorrow: Ganesh Chaturthi: the moon that laughed

segments.voice: Yesterday: the driver. Krishna chose to hold the reins for Arjuna, and the stories camp closed. Today, the driver's first night.

A prison cell in the city of Mathura. Midnight, a storm outside. A mother, Devaki, and a father, Vasudeva, in chains. Her brother, the tyrant king Kamsa, was told at her wedding that her eighth child would kill him. So he locked them up and took every baby they had. Now the eighth is coming. Last time, Krishna was a grown man holding a chariot's reins; tonight's festival goes back to the very start. And the whole night is one question: can a newborn be carried out of a locked prison, across a flooding river, before morning?
screen: `A PRISON AT MIDNIGHT.` → `KAMSA FEARS THE EIGHTH CHILD.` → `CAN A BABY GET OUT BY MORNING?`

segments.voice: The Bhagavata Purana tells it like this. At midnight, the baby is born. The guards fall into a deep sleep. The chains fall from Vasudeva's wrists. The prison doors swing open on their own. Vasudeva puts his newborn son in a basket on his head and walks out into the storm, to the river Yamuna, in flood. And the river, in the story, lets him through; in a popular telling, the water rises to touch the baby's feet, then parts. The great serpent Shesha rises behind him and spreads his many hoods over the basket like an umbrella against the rain. On the far side, in the village of Gokul, the cowherd's wife Yashoda has just given birth to a daughter. Vasudeva quietly swaps the babies and walks back to his cell. In the morning Kamsa comes for the child, and the baby girl slips from his hands, rises into the sky as a goddess, and tells him: the one you fear is already born, somewhere else. That's Janmashtami: janma, birth, and ashtami, the eighth day of the moon's dark half, when tradition says he was born. Households that keep the festival fast all day and stay up until midnight, singing, and at the hour of the birth they ring bells and rock a tiny cradle. This is the Hindu teaching of the avatar: God coming down into the world. In the Gita, Krishna says he comes, age after age, whenever goodness declines. And look where he arrives: not a palace, a prison cell, at the darkest hour. Many devotees read the midnight vigil that way: God comes into the dark, not after it.
screen: `THE CHAINS FALL, THE DOORS OPEN.` · `THE RIVER PARTS; THE SERPENT SHELTERS.` · `JANMA + ASHTAMI: BIRTH ON THE EIGHTH.` · `AVATAR: GOD COMES DOWN.` · then, large: `THE AVATAR COMES IN THE DARKEST HOUR.`

segments.voice: Dim the lights or close your eyes. If you pray, ring a bell once, or say softly Jai Shri Krishna, the way families do at midnight, and picture a tiny cradle rocking. If you don't pray, sit in the dark with something good you're still waiting for. Let the waiting be here, the way the family waited in the cell. Then picture one small light, the door opening a crack.
Janmashtami. Janma, birth; ashtami, the eighth day. The midnight birthday of Krishna.
Your line: the avatar comes in the darkest hour. Krishna chose a prison at midnight. Happy Janmashtami.

howItsDone: On Janmashtami many Hindus fast until midnight, sing devotional songs, and at the hour of Krishna's birth ring bells and rock a small cradle holding an image of baby Krishna; in Maharashtra the next day, teams form human pyramids to break a pot of curds hung high, as Krishna the butter thief would.

original.note: Sanskrit: janma (birth) + ashtami (the eighth day of a lunar fortnight).

Mathura.meaning: the city where Krishna was born in Kamsa's prison

Kamsa.meaning: the tyrant king, Devaki's brother, who feared her eighth child

Yamuna.meaning: the river Vasudeva crossed in flood with the baby

Gokul.meaning: the cowherd village where Krishna grew up in hiding

Yashoda.meaning: the cowherd's wife who raised Krishna as her own

Shesha.meaning: the great many-hooded serpent who sheltered the baby

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.1–10.4 (Kamsa, Devaki and Vasudeva; Krishna's birth; the crossing to Gokul; Yogamaya)
